newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to sell 100 firms with World Bank support.
newsitem.headline: Romania to sell 100 firms with World Bank support.

text.p: Romania's State Ownership Fund (FPS) said on Wednesday it planned to use World Bank assistance to privatise 100 state-owned companies.
"The FPS will select 100 Romanian firms to be privatised with World Bank assistance," FPS president Sorin Dimitriu told a news conference after a seminar on privatisation.
"Those companies should be attractive and have a letter of intent from foreign investors," Dimitriu said, but gave no further details.
World Bank officials were not immediately available for comment.
On Wednesday, Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, who heads the centrist-coalition government, said Romania has privatised about 800 state companies in the past four months.
The core of Ciorbea's reform programme is faster privatisation and restructuring, which had been sluggish under the former leftists ousted in last year's elections.

The World Bank, committed to supporting Romania's reforms, approved on Wednesday a $550 million credit package for the Balkan country, including loans for agriculture restructuring, social security and highway upgrading.
By end-1996 Romania had privatised only about 3,100 companies from over 6,000 state-run firms.
